segments.title: Hiroshima as a thriving city beside its memorials
segments.summary: A view from the memorial area prompts a reflection on Hiroshima as a thriving, rebuilt city whose memorials preserve the memory of the bombing.
segments.body: The visit overturns an expectation that Hiroshima would be defined by the atomic bombing. The city makes an impression through its thriving community, beauty, and extensive rebuilding. The view from the memorial near the dome is recalled through an image of space scooped out by the bomb, with the rebuilt city beyond it. Commemoration and recovery occupy the same urban landscape. The museum's simple presentation is remembered as one of the most emotionally effective ever encountered.

evidence.note: He contrasts an expectation of a city defined by its past with the thriving city seen from the memorial area and calls the museum devastatingly effective.

segments.title: Museum objects and the human cost of the Hiroshima bombing
segments.summary: The Hiroshima museum makes the bombing's human cost immediate through a girl's experience of cancer after the attack and a school uniform assembled from pieces belonging to three children who died.
segments.body: Familiar facts and figures about the bombing feel different when encountered through the museum's objects and personal stories. One account concerns a girl who developed cancer after the bomb and still tried to keep others happy. A small schoolboy's uniform assembled from surviving clothing pieces belonging to three children who died has even greater emotional force. Its resemblance to a remembered primary-school uniform makes the victims imaginable as ordinary school friends. This personal reflection on civilian suffering concentrates on the emotional impact of the exhibits.

evidence.note: He contrasts familiar facts and figures with the story of a girl who developed cancer after the bombing and a schoolboy's uniform assembled from surviving clothing pieces belonging to three children who died. The uniform reminds him of his primary-school uniform and friends.
